ns2:section.sectionText: Topic: Ordinary Objects. We will examine some issues in material-object metaphysics centering on the question of what sorts of highly visible, macroscopic things there are? Eliminativists maintain that there are far fewer than we ordinarily take there to be. Permissivists maintain that there are far more things, right before our eyes, than we ordinarily take there to be. Our aim is to assess the viability of a conservative view, which permits only ordinary objects and nothing out of the ordinary. We will survey the main arguments for eliminativism and permissivism?concerning vagueness, arbitrariness, causation, persistence, and identity?and the wide range of responses to these arguments. We will also examine the status of the intuitions that underwrite the conservative view, by examining attempts to explain away or debunk these intuitions. This section is letter-graded for 4-hour credit. 500-level courses are graduate courses, and are intended for graduate students only.
